claims.text: IS FAIR and KFUPM Key Rules for Students (compiled PDF)

evidence.quote:
A student cheats or assists in cheating in coursework or quizzes
1. The course instructor assigns the student a grade of zero for that work.
2. The instructor submits a report with details of the case and recommendations to the Department Chair.
3. The Department Chair forwards the recommendations to the College Dean.
4. The College Council reviews the case and takes one of the following actions:
• Reconsider the penalty.
• Confirm the penalty.
• Assign a grade of Denial (DN) for the course.
• The College Council may also refer the case to the Student Affairs Committee, which will investigate further and submit recommendations to the University President in accordance with the Student Disciplinary Regulations. The student may appeal the decision to the Dean of Student Affairs within one week of being notified.

evidence.quote:
A student cheats, attempts to cheat, or assists in cheating during any written examination (Major, Midterm, or Final Exam)
1. The course instructor assigns the student a grade of zero for that work.
2. The instructor submits a report with details of the case and recommendations to the Department Chair.
3. The Department Chair forwards the recommendations to the College Dean.
4. The College Council reviews the case and takes one of the following actions:
• Reconsider the penalty.
• Confirm the penalty.
• Assign a grade of Denial (DN) for the course.
• The College Council may also refer the case to the Student Affairs Committee, which will investigate further and submit recommendations to the University President in accordance with the Student Disciplinary Regulations. The student may appeal the decision to the Dean of Student Affairs within one week of being notified.
Note: In addition to the Denial (DN) grade, the Student Affairs Committee generally recommends a disciplinary penalty not less than suspension for one academic semester.

evidence.quote:
Article 12:
First: Appeals Related to Academic Matters
1. If a student disputes the grade awarded in any course (final exam, midterm, research, or other academic requirements), they must first discuss the matter with the course instructor. If unresolved, the matter may be escalated to the Academic Department Chair with supporting reasons, within one week of the following semester or from the time of receiving the grade. Beyond this period, the right to appeal is forfeited.
2. The Department Chair shall form a committee, chaired by the Chair, to review the matter. The committee may recommend upholding the grade, rejecting it entirely, or modifying it (positively or negatively), with justification. The recommendation is then submitted to the College Dean, who refers it to the College Council for a final decision.
3. The Department Chair must inform the student in writing of the College Council’s decision within one week of its issuance.

Article 4:
Disciplinary penalties include:
1. Verbal or written warning, or a written pledge.
2. Written reprimand.
3. Mandatory community service for a specified number of hours.
4. Deprivation of certain student services, housing, or student activities for one semester, less, more, or permanently.
5. Financial fine.
6. Cancellation of grades in one or more courses, with failure recorded.
7. Suspension from study for one or more regular or summer semesters.
8. Permanent dismissal from the University and termination of enrollment.
9. Any other penalties approved by the University President.
Article 5:
Penalties must be proportionate to the severity of the violation, considering previous infractions and surrounding circumstances.
